title: Nanduti (spider-web lace)
summary: Ñandutí, the Guaraní word for spider web, is a needle lace of Paraguay worked on a stretched frame: fine threads are laid out as sixteen rays from a centre and then stitched ring by ring into suns, flowers and webs, often in bright colours.
howToPlay: Choose a thread colour and a stitch from the strip under the disc.
Tap a sector of the lace disc: the same stitch appears in every sector that matches it as the disc turns.
Match the small disc shown above, then press Check.
rules: The disc has sixteen rays and six rings, and its design repeats eight times around the centre, like a web worked outward from the middle.
A sector counts only when its stitch and its thread colour both match the design.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you may undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Ñandutí is made by women of Paraguay, with the town of Itauguá long known as its home, and has been handed down since the colonial period; each round motif is only a few centimetres across and many are joined into larger cloths.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original, after radial web medallions)
